stories.title: Nijmegen moves dikes to create space for river flooding
stories.summary: Following floods in the 1990s, the Netherlands implemented the Room for the River program to expand flood drainage space. In Nijmegen, the city moved the Lent dike inland by 350 meters and excavated a 3-kilometer channel. The project aims to reduce flood risks in riverside residential areas.

stories.title: Cities pilot heat resilience strategies under AMRUT 2.0
stories.summary: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has launched a pilot programme to help 12 Indian cities address urban heat risks. Participating cities are exploring innovative solutions to protect vulnerable communities. The programme aims to identify and implement city-level interventions to mitigate the impacts of rising temperatures.

stories.title: India rises in green transition ranking despite coal rebound
stories.summary: India reached 45th in the Allianz Green Transition Tracker 2026 as emissions fell 0.2% last year. While low-carbon electricity share increased, coal generation rebounded in 2026. Fossil fuel subsidies have more than doubled since 2015, raising questions about the sustainability of the country's emissions decline.

stories.title: Department of Financial Services claims solar award
stories.summary: The Department of Financial Services achieved 100% solarisation across all feasible administrative buildings, commissioning 61.50 MW of capacity across 2,576 sites. The achievement earned the PM Surya Ghar Excellence Award. The department identified 4,144 buildings in total, but only those deemed feasible were included.

stories.title: Defence ministry halts Mumbai construction projects
stories.summary: The defence ministry has ordered an immediate halt to construction projects near defence establishments in Mumbai that lack necessary approvals. The order affects numerous ongoing developments, particularly in suburban areas like Malad-Kandivli. Developers and homebuyers are now facing what the industry calls deepening uncertainty.

stories.title: Enforcement Directorate charges Raheja Developers
stories.summary: The Enforcement Directorate has filed a charge sheet against Raheja Developers and its promoters for alleged money laundering. The agency seeks the confiscation of assets worth Rs 2,399.65 crore, citing the diversion of funds paid by homebuyers who never received possession of their properties.

stories.summary: Top 10 Best Architecture Firms In India In 2027 Top 10 Best Architecture Firms in India in 2027 Architecture in India is undergoing a significant transformation as cities expand, infrastructure development accelerates, commercial real estate grows, and demand for sustainable residential and institutional spaces increases.

stories.title: ZAO completes concrete art center in Rizhao
stories.summary: ZAO has finished the Rizhao Community Art Center in Shandong province. The building features an upper volume supported at three corners, with eye-shaped openings carved through the level beneath. It sits beside a wooded hillside and a small lake. The structure appears to hover above the landscape.

stories.title: SABO Project renovates Manhattan apartment
stories.summary: SABO Project has renovated a 728-square-foot apartment on Manhattan’s Lower East Side for a family of three. The design includes rounded partitions and green accents to soften divisions between functional areas. The studio says the layout allows the central living room to extend into surrounding alcoves.

stories.title: Sharjah Architecture Triennial 2026 examines global urbanism
stories.summary: The Sharjah Architecture Triennial 2026 is exploring the concept of Architecture Otherwise. The event focuses on the scale of human endeavor and the environmental impact of design. It aims to scrutinize the view that everything is architecture, while addressing the responsibility designers hold toward the planet.

stories.title: Aedas completes pebble-shaped port in Shenzhen
stories.summary: Aedas has opened a nine-story immigration hub on the Shenzhen River to replace the 1989 Huanggang Port. The design uses a river pebble as its guiding image, incorporating transport links and public space for 200,000 daily passengers. The building treats the act of crossing as a fluid experience.

stories.title: Taller Alberto Calleja completes Casa Nova in Mexico
stories.summary: Taller Alberto Calleja has finished Casa Nova, a holiday home in Mazunte, Oaxaca. The project features two concrete volumes separated by a tree-filled fissure that frames views of the sea. Elevated timber walkways bridge the gap between the structures, which are situated on a narrow coastal site.

stories.title: SOM masterplans coastal city in Egypt
stories.summary: SOM has released a master plan for Alam Al Roum, a 20.6-square-kilometer city on Egypt’s Mediterranean coast. The design features 22 kilometers of seawater-connected lagoons intended to act as natural buffers against the sea. The plan treats the shoreline as an adaptive space rather than a fixed edge.

stories.title: Peter Morris completes pink Cloud House in London
stories.summary: Architect Peter Morris has finished The Cloud House in North London, featuring a facade of enormous arches and scalloped rooflines. The project combines Miami pastels with grey brick surroundings. The architect describes the result as somewhere between a Gothic church and a Miami beachfront hotel.

stories.title: Powerhouse Parramatta museum set to open
stories.summary: The Powerhouse Parramatta museum in Sydney is scheduled to open tomorrow. Designed by Moreau Kusunoki and Genton, the building uses a steel lattice exoskeleton as both facade and structure. The project is described as the largest cultural investment in Australia since the Sydney Opera House.

stories.title: Homeowner questions spray foam installation quality
stories.summary: A homeowner in climate zone 7 is seeking advice on a closed-cell spray foam installation that failed to meet the specified 3.5-inch depth. The contractor has offered to apply additional foam to reach the target thickness. The homeowner is concerned about whether the material cured correctly.

stories.title: New York homeowner weighs attic insulation options
stories.summary: A homeowner in Westchester County is deciding between blown-in cellulose or closed-cell spray foam for an unfinished attic. The primary concerns include moisture management, roof durability, and wood rot prevention. The home recently received a new roof, and the owner is looking to maximize the lifespan of the investment.

stories.title: Gliese Design releases 3D-printed collection
stories.summary: Gliese Design has launched the Ondu Wonderland Collection, featuring a 3D-printed table lamp, vase, and candle holder. The objects use sustainable biopolymers and additive manufacturing to create ruffled, Victorian-inspired forms. The studio describes the series as a blend of Baroque aesthetics and sci-fi influences.

stories.title: Review examines 3D-printed acoustic panels
stories.summary: A review in Frontiers in Mechanical Engineering analyzes 3D-printed acoustic panels, noting that additive manufacturing allows for complex lattice and metamaterial structures. The study synthesizes literature from 1980 to 2026, identifying key design variables for sound-absorbing performance that are difficult to achieve through conventional manufacturing methods.

stories.title: Callaway Golf to open 3D printing factory in Texas
stories.summary: Callaway Golf plans to invest $15 million in a 3D printing facility in Fort Worth, Texas. The company intends to produce clubs in-house to iterate designs faster and respond to market demand. The move follows industry-wide experimentation with 3D-printed components in golf equipment.

stories.title: Brooklyn brownstone owner seeks air sealing advice
stories.summary: A homeowner in Brooklyn is working to improve the air sealing of a townhouse. The project involves addressing a gap between the top of a brick wall and the roof deck. The owner is looking for methods to prevent cold air from entering through the roof joist area.

stories.title: Massachusetts homeowner asks about hybrid spray foam
stories.summary: A homeowner in Massachusetts is considering a hybrid spray foam approach for an unvented attic to prevent ice dams. The plan involves 2 inches of closed-cell foam combined with open-cell foam. The owner is seeking a professional assessment before starting the project in early December.

stories.title: 3D printer guide for home repairs
stories.summary: A guide to 3D printers highlights their utility for creating replacement parts, such as a bathroom sink assembly. The author notes that 3D printing provides an at-home solution when hardware stores are inaccessible. The piece suggests that 3D printers are useful tools for crafting and creating.

stories.title: Chaos updates V-Ray with AI tools
stories.summary: Chaos has updated its V-Ray Collection to include AI-driven guidance, 3D asset generation, and support for the Model Context Protocol. The update aims to automate time-consuming tasks in visualization workflows. Users can now connect external AI assistants like ChatGPT directly to the rendering software.

stories.title: Telangana plans climate resilience with bamboo and policy
stories.summary: Telangana is launching a project pipeline worth ₹20,000 crore to climate-proof its cities. The plan includes bamboo bus shelters and a mandatory Urban Road Code to integrate climate concerns into municipal services. The state aims to complete this under its Telangana Rising 2047 vision.

stories.title: Maharashtra revives historic stepwells to combat drought
stories.summary: Maharashtra is investing Rs 25 crore to restore 75 historic stepwells, known as baravs, to address recurring water shortages. The initiative aims to repurpose traditional infrastructure that has fallen out of use. The state is looking to the past to solve its modern water security problems.

stories.title: Urban wetlands face rapid degradation in Indian cities
stories.summary: Metropolitan expansion is converting marshes and floodplains into housing and commercial projects, threatening urban resilience. Wetlands are often treated as wasteland, leading to the severance of feeder channels and habitat isolation. These areas serve as essential stopover habitats for migratory species and provide critical ecosystem services.

stories.title: Telangana secures more central urban infrastructure funding
stories.summary: The Union ministry of housing and urban affairs approved five additional projects for Telangana, bringing total sanctioned investments under the Urban Challenge Fund to ₹9,573 crore. The projects include flood mitigation for Warangal and an expansion of Hyderabad's water scheme. The state has secured ₹2,293 crore in central support.

stories.title: Agartala reviews sewage upgrades during election period
stories.summary: Tripura’s Chief Secretary chaired a high-level meeting to accelerate sewage network upgrades under the Agartala Smart City Project. The review focused on completing infrastructure work before municipal polling day. The administration noted that timely progress could help address drainage concerns and strengthen sanitation facilities across the city.

stories.title: Kanpur Metro builds steel arch bridge to clear highway
stories.summary: Kanpur Metro is constructing a 67.5-metre steel arch bridge to carry Corridor 2 over a busy highway. The Open Web Truss Girder design allows the bridge to span the road without a central pillar. The construction team is currently using temporary steel supports to hold the frame.

stories.title: Bengaluru airport metro construction causes traffic delays
stories.summary: Commuters heading to Kempegowda International Airport face 18 months of traffic restrictions on Ballari Road due to Namma Metro Blue Line construction. The line, connecting Central Silk Board to the airport, is expected to become fully operational by March 2028. Construction work has already begun.

stories.title: Varanasi ropeway nears completion to cut travel time
stories.summary: Varanasi is finishing India's first urban public transport ropeway, with trial runs underway on the 3.85-km Rathyatra-Godowlia stretch. The project aims to reduce travel time between the railway station and Godowlia from 45 minutes to 15 minutes. Approximately 95% of the construction is now complete.

stories.title: Bay Area voters approve transit tax to avoid funding crisis
stories.summary: Voters in the San Francisco Bay Area approved new sales taxes to generate $1bn annually for regional transit operators. The measure passed with 62.2% support across five counties. Advocates hope the funding will prevent a potential death spiral for the region's financially distressed public transit agencies.

stories.title: Rawalpindi officials discuss water and flooding issues
stories.summary: Officials from the Water and Sanitation Agency met with the Rawalpindi Chamber of Commerce to discuss municipal challenges. The agency manages water supply for 1.8 million people using 500 tube wells. The meeting addressed ongoing water shortages and urban flooding concerns within the city's 90-square-kilometre service area.

stories.summary: RAWALPINDI: Water and Sanitation Agency (Wasa) officials met Rawalpindi Chamber of Commerce and Industry (RCCI) office-bearers on Thursday to discuss water shortage, urban flooding and ongoing municipal challenges. stories.title: Paisley library conversion shortlisted for architecture award
stories.summary: Collective Architecture has converted a dilapidated building in Paisley, Scotland, into a public library. The project, which features reading and event spaces, is shortlisted for the 2026 RIAS Andrew Doolan Best Building in Scotland Award. The design aims to serve as a welcoming community space.

stories.title: UN climate summit faces modest progress expectations
stories.summary: The UN climate summit in Antalya begins amid wars and energy insecurity, complicating efforts for collective climate action. While renewable energy is presented as a security route, the summit's ambitious agenda faces modest prospects. Developing countries continue to seek greater finance and support to address climate damage.

stories.title: Super El Niño expected to peak in December
stories.summary: A rapidly developing super El Niño is on track to peak at the end of 2026, potentially pushing global temperatures to record levels next year. Climate models and datasets suggest the pattern is significant. Dr Zeke Hausfather described the current climate event as simply staggering.

stories.title: Construction robot startups raised $1.6 billion this year
stories.summary: Construction and robotics companies raised $1.6 billion through October 29, more than 4x the $389 million recorded in all of 2025, according to Crunchbase data. The funding went into 30 rounds, compared to 28 last year. Bedrock Robotics accounted for 54 percent of the total.

stories.summary: Physicl closed a $10 million round to address the gap between simulated training and real-world performance. The startup repurposes e-commerce product display technology to build hyper-accurate digital twins for AI training. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.summary: Nov 06: Singapore is accelerating its efforts to modernise the construction industry through robotics, automation and artificial intelligence. stories.title: Glyph (1) uses orientation as an interface
stories.summary: Designer Adam Miklosi released Glyph (1), a six-sided cube that replaces screens with orientation-based interaction. Each face features a programmable LED matrix, allowing users to trigger AI functions by rotating the device. The value of the interaction is determined by which face points upward.

stories.title: Chaos integrates AI into Enscape workflow
stories.summary: Chaos has updated Enscape to version 4.22, integrating the AI tool Veras 2.0 directly into the interface. The update allows architects to generate design variations and experiment with materials without opening a separate window. The software aims to incorporate AI into existing visualisation workflows.

stories.title: Bihar Museum ranked among world top 10
stories.summary: The Bihar Museum has been ranked ninth in the 2026 edition of the World’s 100 Best Museums by Worth a Journey. Designed by architect Fumihiko Maki and opened in 2017, the structure was built in concrete and stone to reflect the state's cultural ambitions.

stories.summary: The U.S. Department of State selected the University of Miami School of Architecture to curate the 2027 U.S. Pavilion. Led by Germane Barnes and Vyta Pivo, the exhibition, titled Earth Craft, will explore the history of building materials including brick, rammed earth, adobe, and concrete masonry.

stories.summary: The University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa School of Architecture is offering six graduate assistantships for the 2027 academic year. The positions include a 100 percent tuition exemption and an annual stipend of $31,524. Applications for the program are due January 1, 2027.

stories.summary: Harvard student Radhika Saran and her team won the Global Medical category of the James Dyson Award 2026 for Rumble Rims, a headset designed to screen for concussion symptoms. The team received a $40,000 cash prize for the healthcare technology innovation.

research.title: Human bodies produce 2 billion metric tons of CO2 a year just by staying alive
research.summary: Humans collectively produce more than 2 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide annually just by turning food into energy, a 74% increase over three decades largely driven by population growth. Unlike fossil fuel emissions, however, the CO2 we exhale is part of the natural carbon cycle, and scientists say.

research.title: Scientists discover Europe's ancient forests were nothing like we imagined
research.summary: Scientists have uncovered evidence that Europe was dominated for more than 20 million years by open woodlands, colorful meadows, and large grazing animals, not the dense forests long considered its natural state. The surprising discovery challenges modern reforestation strategies, suggesting that planting thick forests could actually harm the.

research.title: Scientists accidentally solve a chemistry mystery that lasted 60 years
research.summary: After more than 60 years of unsuccessful attempts, scientists have finally isolated stable examples of elusive boron-oxygen molecules once considered too unstable to capture. The surprising breakthrough, achieved using relatively simple chemical reactions, could pave the way for an entirely new class of exotic compounds.

research.title: Something strange is happening beneath a volcano near 2 million people
research.summary: Scientists have discovered evidence of two hidden magma sources beneath Nicaragua’s Masaya volcano, where satellite observations revealed mysterious ground movements suggesting magma is shifting deep underground. The findings could improve eruption forecasting for the active volcano, which sits near 2 million people and attracts tourists to its spectacular.

research.title: NASA discovers hidden fires burning beneath the Amazon rainforest
research.summary: El Niño is fueling a dangerous cascade of wildfires across the tropics, with the Amazon rainforest now experiencing widespread burning and scientists warning that the worst may still be ahead. NASA researchers are uncovering dozens of previously undetected fires, suggesting the destruction could be even more extensive than.

research.title: Scientists discover a surprising twist in Japan's 7,300-year-old volcanic apocalypse
research.summary: A catastrophic volcanic eruption 7,300 years ago devastated Japan, but new research reveals that its impact on prehistoric populations was far more complex than previously believed. While some communities disappeared or declined, others unexpectedly flourished as survivors migrated, adapted, and found new ways to thrive.

research.title: Scientists who discovered a third form of magnetism win major physics prize
research.summary: Physicists have uncovered a hidden third form of magnetism that challenges more than 100 years of established physics. Called altermagnetism, the discovery could transform future computing and electronics while opening an entirely new frontier in quantum research.
